name: Non-profit, association or club
description: A charity, association, foundation or sports or hobby club: events, documents such as the statutes and annual reports, the board and contacts and members' questions, with facts about the legal form, registration, donations, the membership fee and volunteering.

questions.question: What is the legal form of your organisation?
questions.help: As it is registered, e.g. "registered association" or "foundation". Mention a charitable or public-benefit status only if an authority has granted it.

questions.question: Where is the organisation registered, and under what number?
questions.help: As in your documents, e.g. the entry in the register of associations or the charity number. A company ID, if you have one, belongs in Business details.

questions.question: In which year was the organisation founded?
Where does the organisation work?
questions.help: For example "the town and the surrounding villages" or "across the country".

questions.question: Can people donate online? Give the address of the donation page.
questions.help: Your own payment page or a donation platform; the Donate buttons lead here. Talea itself takes no payments. Leave it empty if you do not collect donations online.

questions.question: Which bank account should donations go to?
questions.help: The organisation's public account for donations, exactly as on your documents, with the reference donors should use if any. Leave it empty if you do not publish one.

questions.question: Is there a membership fee? How much, and how is it paid?
questions.help: For example "30 EUR a year, students 15 EUR, by bank transfer by the end of March". Leave it empty if membership is free.

questions.question: Who should people write to if they want to volunteer?
questions.help: An e-mail address that someone reads regularly.

audit.message: Publish the statutes and the latest annual report as documents – members and donors look for them; check whether your law requires publishing them.
No document has changed for over a year – publish the latest annual report.
Introduce the board and the contact people – members, donors and partners want to know who runs the organisation.
State where the organisation is registered – donors and partners check who they are dealing with.
Add a contact e-mail in Business details – people who want to join or help need a way to reach you.

claude: Members, volunteers, donors and partners come to see what the organisation does, who runs it, how to join, help or give, and whether it can be trusted – put the mission in plain words, the next events and clear ways to join, volunteer and donate on the home page. Statutes, annual reports and minutes are the documents collection, the board and contacts the team, activities the events. Never invent impact figures, members, beneficiaries, partners, grants, awards, testimonials or how donations are spent – ask the owner and cite the annual report. Do not say donations are tax-deductible or that the organisation has a charitable or public-benefit status unless the owner confirms it, and say such rules should be checked. Donate buttons lead to {{fact.donation_url}}; Talea takes no payments. Photos of people, children above all, only with consent.
